shape: a parent's odd habit that the child only understands years later

slides.text: in our first flat, you always left the stove light on before going to bed.
i switched it off every night, annoyed at the meter eating our pound coins.
so we spent winter in that small fight, you turning it on, me clicking it off.
but the night i lost my job, i walked home in the cold past midnight.
the stairs were pitch black, and i stood outside the door for five minutes, too tired to turn the key.
when i pushed it open, that thin yellow strip was already sitting on the kitchen lino.
[[you were never forgetful.]] you just didn't want me walking into a dark flat.

caption:
we were nineteen and arguing over fifty pence on the electric meter.
you never once explained why you kept turning it back on.
send this to the roommate who always left a light burning for your late shift.

alt: a seven-slide story about an old roommate who always left the stove light on at night, and what that quiet habit actually meant.

you never went to sleep without leaving the stove light on.
